description: A story-battle talk set: an ordered list of BattleTalk rows, gated by parallel battle-log conditions for normal mission waves, with cue sheets preloaded for its dialogue. The same rows are also queued directly by hardcoded tutorial steps.

Id.technical: FName declared as Id; the export spells the key ID and uses it as the DataTable import key. Normal callers pass an external SetId from StoryMissionWave.Id_BattleTalkSet or a tutorial builder and resolve the first matching table in DTM.BattleTalkSetDataTables (+0xB30). The row's own Id is read only after playback, when FStudioBattleSystem330 passes CurrentSet->Id through NotifyBattleTalkEnd to every character's OnBattleTalkEnd. The observed CP_020 override increments a counter; the other reconstructed controllers use the no-op base implementation.

CueSheetName.simple: Cue sheets whose audio should be preloaded for this set.
CueSheetName.technical: TArray<FName>. For the current story mission and retry-indexed wave, StudioBattleNotify368 walks each referenced set, skips None, and appends these names to StudioCueSheetNames_C20; the base phase then calls AGameSoundManager::LoadCueSheets, which de-duplicates names and loads each sheet. The exported values are CRI cue-sheet names and all match VoiceDataTable.CueSheetName values, but they are not Voice row IDs and are not derived from Id_BattleTalk: PlayVoiceById separately resolves each talk's Id_Voice to a Voice row. In the supplied export the first six tutorial sets contain only None placeholders; the other sets list one or two names.

Id_BattleTalk.simple: Ordered list of BattleTalkDataTable rows to play.
Id_BattleTalk.technical: TArray<FName>. QueueBattleTalkSet resolves the first set row in DTM.BattleTalkSetDataTables, clears the playback queue, skips None, and for each remaining ID takes the first BattleTalk row across DTM.BattleTalkDataTables (+0xB40); unresolved IDs are dropped and queue order is array order. If no rows resolve it returns without starting playback and does not try a later duplicate set table; otherwise it disables character battle voice, stores CurrentSet, sets bWaitForInput and starts Queue[0]. Both mission-wave paths pass bWaitForInput=false; tutorial steps pass true. The story phase independently walks the same IDs to add direct or variation-derived portrait textures to the preload list. Exported rows have 20 slots with 1-15 non-None IDs followed by None padding.

ValueType.simple: Battle-log statistic (or None for unconditional) for each condition slot.
ValueType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogValueType>, indexed in lockstep with TargetType/PassiveType/Value/ConditionType. Only this array classifies a set: FBattleStoryState_Fight::Enter queues a set when every ValueType entry is None (an empty array would also qualify), while Tick evaluates each non-None entry. Invalid is also non-None and therefore makes a set conditional, then EvaluateLog rejects it. EvaluateLog(..., false) reads RoundLogs rather than TotalLogs, requires a valid player and at least one candidate character, and returns false when no log entry exists. SumLogValues sums across those characters except CursedEnergy_Level (maximum) and HitPointRate (average by candidate count). No exported row uses Invalid.

TargetType.simple: Whose log value is measured: ally, self, enemy, or None.
TargetType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogTargetType> read at the same index as ValueType and passed to EvaluateLog. Ally collects the player's team using GAISlot001() as the team; Myself is only PlayerCharacter; Enemy is the player's rival team. After the player-validity check, None, Invalid and any unrecognized value leave the candidate list empty, so SumLogValues is not called and the condition fails.

PassiveType.simple: Whether the measured value was sent or received by the target.
PassiveType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogPassiveType> forwarded to EvaluateLog at the same index. SumLogValues selects ReceiveValues only for Receive; None, Send, Invalid and any other value use SendValues, then look up the ValueType key in that map. Exported conditional slots use Send or Receive; the None values in unconditional slots are never evaluated.

Value.simple: Numeric threshold compared against the measured log value.
Value.technical: TArray<float> of inclusive thresholds: Success_GreaterThanEquals passes when the evaluated log value >= Value[Index], and Success_LessThanEquals when it is <=. Units are those of the selected ValueType; there is no unit field. Exported conditional rows use HitPointRate fractions (0.5-0.75; averaged per candidate), TimeLimit in seconds of elapsed battle time (10/60/120; the logged TimeLimit field is elapsed time, not remaining time), and count/gauge thresholds of 1 or 2. Unconditional slots are 0.0 and ignored; every exported row has two threshold slots, of which only slot 0 is used.

ConditionType.simple: Comparison operator that decides whether a condition passes.
ConditionType.technical: TArray<EGameBattleLogConditionType> consulted only after EvaluateLog succeeds. In the reconstructed consumer only Success_GreaterThanEquals and Success_LessThanEquals add credit; None, Invalid and both Failure_* members fall through with no credit. Conditions counts every ValueType != None (including Invalid), and the set is queued only when Conditions > 0 && Conditions <= Held, so one failed lookup or comparison prevents a conditional set from firing. All exported conditional slots use a Success_* member and every second slot is None.

notes: The five condition arrays are parallel, not nested structs: consumers index them by the same integer and take Set->ValueType.Num() as the condition count. Mismatched array lengths in an asset could therefore produce out-of-bounds reads; no validation was observed.

In the single supplied export all 79 rows have exactly two cue-sheet slots, 20 talk slots and two condition slots, every row ID matches its row key, 27 rows have one active condition and 52 are unconditional, and the second condition slot is always None/0.0.

Conditional classification uses ValueType only. Fight enter queues unconditional sets, while Tick queues conditional sets only while IsBattleTalkEnabled; both paths suppress repeats through QueuedBattleTalkSets and add the ID immediately after calling QueueBattleTalkSet, even if no talk rows resolve. Hardcoded tutorial steps are a third entry path that bypasses the condition arrays.

All consumers walk the DTM table arrays in order and take the first hit, with FindRow warnings disabled. DTM.BattleTalkSetDataTables is populated by resolving the DataTable primary asset through the asset manager and filtering out null tables.

The constructor is empty, so the row struct supplies no code defaults; all exported values come from the asset. FName None is the sentinel talk/cue ID, and the battle-log enums include explicit None and Invalid(255) members.

Failure_GreaterThanEquals, Failure_LessThanEquals and Invalid have no case in the reconstructed ConditionType switch, and no exported row uses them. A retail Blueprint-specific meaning cannot be assigned from the available evidence.

StoryMissionWave.Id_BattleTalkSet is the normal join into this table: 74 non-None references occur in the 93 exported wave rows, 73 resolve to set rows, and STMSN_03036M_01_02 has no set row (it is also the key of a BattleTalk row). The six STMSN_01000M_0* sets are absent from wave references but are hardcoded into the reconstructed tutorial builder.

CueSheetName values are cue-sheet names that match VoiceDataTable.CueSheetName and reach LoadCueSheets; they are not Voice row IDs and are not used to look up Voice rows. Voice playback follows BattleTalk.Id_Voice through PlayVoiceById.

Runtime behavior here is reconstructed from retail code and checked against the supplied exports. Retail Blueprint graphs were not available; the project guidance says Blueprints are data-only, so no independent retail Blueprint behavior is asserted.

usages.detail: Requests BattleTalkSetDataTable as a DataTable primary asset.
Resolves the loaded table into DTM.BattleTalkSetDataTables (+0xB30); null tables are filtered.
Fight enter looks up wave-referenced sets and queues those with no non-None ValueType.
Fight tick looks up sets and evaluates their parallel battle-log condition arrays while IsBattleTalkEnabled.
QueueBattleTalkSet resolves the first matching set row and its ordered Id_BattleTalk rows.
After the last line, CurrentSet->Id is passed to NotifyBattleTalkEnd.
NotifyBattleTalkEnd forwards the set ID to every character's OnBattleTalkEnd slot.
StudioBattleNotify368 walks wave-referenced sets for CueSheetName preload names.
LoadCueSheets receives the collected cue-sheet names before battle combat assets finish loading.
StudioBattleNotify360 walks Id_BattleTalk rows to preload talk portrait textures.
The reconstructed tutorial builder hardcodes STMSN_01000M_01 and similar set IDs as tutorial talk steps.
TutorialTalk queues each hardcoded set with bWaitForInput=true.
